title: Hybrid sparse-lexical + dense-cosine retrieval: does changing the scoring function break the exact-cosine recall tie?

prereg.claim_under_test: Every engine measured in scratch/refound ties at 60.6 evidence-recall@4 on n71433 because they all compute the same exact cosine. A lexical arm fused with that cosine is a DIFFERENT scoring function and can therefore break the tie.

baseline.arm: exact dense cosine over the same L2-normalised nomic-embed-text vectors every engine arm uses
baseline.note_on_the_brief: The brief quotes '60.6 / 84.6' for recall@4/@10 at n71433. In competitors_standard_results.json 60.6 is evidence_recall@4 and 84.6 is PER-DOC recall@10; evidence_recall@10 is 71.2. Both metrics are reported here against their own baseline so neither is silently swapped.

prereg.primary_metric: evidence_recall_at_4_pct (ALL gold paragraphs inside top-4) -- the metric whose value is the cited 60.6

n71433.questions: hotpot_train_8k questions 0..499 (the same set bench_competitors.py scores: all gold < n_docs, first 500 in file order)

val1190.role: transfer (parameters chosen on n71433 train questions, applied unchanged)

n10000.role: disclosed-contaminated by inspection (see pre_registration_integrity_disclosure); reported for completeness, carries no weight in the verdict

tuning_pool.disjoint_from_eval_by: index (eval = 0..499) AND by normalised question text (audited, see leak_audit)

bar.statistic: paired bootstrap over questions, 10,000 draws, seed 20260917, of (fused - dense) primary metric
bar.note: Registered BEFORE any hybrid number exists. It is not restated afterwards for any arm, winning or losing.

cost_criteria_registered_up_front.why: A recall win that triples latency or doubles disk is a different decision from one that costs 0.2 ms, so the cost bar is fixed now.
cost_criteria_registered_up_front.ship_if: recall bar passed AND added query latency <= +1.0 ms p50 (i.e. under 2x the cited dense p50) AND index adds <= 25% of the 406.2 MiB nanomem already writes for this corpus

arms: linear z-score with exact backfill (isolates the floor)
prereg.union_rule: fusion ranks the UNION of the two candidate lists only; a document one arm never returned is floored (rrf: 0; min-max: 0.0; z: the z of that arm's weakest returned candidate) -- and the *_backfill arms recompute the true score instead, so the floor is priced separately

pre_registration_integrity_disclosure.what_happened: Before this block was written, a debugging smoke test printed aggregate recall for the dense arm, the BM25 arm and the full config grid on a 200-question subset at corpus size 10,000.
pre_registration_integrity_disclosure.which_questions: the first 200 questions whose gold indices are < 10000; all 200 fall inside the 500-question EVALUATION set (indices 0..499) and 0 of them fall in the tuning pool

what_was_seen.corpus: n10000 only; n71433 and val1190 were NOT scored

pre_registration_integrity_disclosure.why_it_does_not_choose_anything: the config grid (K1_GRID, B_GRID, M_GRID, RRF_C_GRID, W_GRID, CASCADE_C_GRID) and every fusion rule were written before that run and are unchanged; selection is a mechanical argmax over the grid on the DISJOINT tuning pool (questions 500..7999), with no human choice
pre_registration_integrity_disclosure.consequence_applied: n10000 is demoted from 'secondary' to 'disclosed-contaminated by inspection, reported for completeness only'. The primary corpus n71433 and the transfer corpus val1190 were never scored before this registration.

prereg.quarantine: This script can only open the four files in ALLOWED_INPUTS; any other path raises PermissionError. No held-out or quarantined fixture is reachable from this code.

n71433.gold_rule: G[:, :2] from hotpot_train_8k_embeds.npz, first 500 questions with gold < n_docs (identical to bench_competitors.py prep)

n10000.gold_rule: G[:, :2] from hotpot_train_8k_embeds.npz, first 500 questions with gold < n_docs (identical to bench_competitors.py prep)

val1190.role: transfer: k1/b/w/c chosen on the 71,433 train questions, applied unchanged
val1190.gold_rule: supporting facts located by first 80 chars (bench_competitors.py rule)

latency_ms.note: the dense figure here is a plain numpy matvec over 71,433x768 fp32 in this process, NOT nanomem's fp16 mmap scan with the PCA screen; the added_* rows are the ones that transfer

disk.reading: the registered arithmetic passes (12.4% of 406.2 MiB); the same criterion against the vault nanomem actually writes today FAILS (32.9% of 153.05 MiB). The 'disk passes' sub-claim is WITHDRAWN.
disk.provenance_of_this_correction: added after the run by arithmetic on the ALREADY-MEASURED index size (50.39 MiB, costs.bm25_index_disk_MiB_npz). No sweep, no scoring and no measurement was repeated, and no recall number in this file changed. The 153.05 MiB denominator is scratch/refound/sidecar_size_results.json's n71433 total for the shipped default, independently confirmed on disk.

machine.co_tenancy_warning: this machine was running other benchmark processes during the measurement; absolute latency is inflated for BOTH arms, so read the added/dense RATIO, not the absolute ms, and compare the ratio to the cited 1.1494

costs.meets_prereg_cost_bar_note: unchanged and still false: the latency criterion fails at +1.0611 ms against the +1.0 ms bar. What changed is that the disk criterion no longer passes either, once its denominator is the vault nanomem now writes.

analysis.what_this_is: post-hoc DESCRIPTIVE statistics on the same predictions; no new arm, no new selection, registered bar unchanged

pre_committed_single_arm.rule: the config with the highest evidence_recall@4 on the tuning pool -- the one arm a caller who had to pick before seeing the eval set would have shipped

multiplicity.adjustment: Bonferroni: per-arm two-sided level 0.05/7, i.e. a 99.29% bootstrap interval

verdict.one_line: The tie DOES break -- fusing a stdlib BM25 arm with the same exact cosine gains +5.0 to +6.2 evidence-recall@10 points at 71,433 docs (95% CI lower bounds +2.6 to +4.0, still positive after Bonferroni over 7 families) -- but on the registered PRIMARY metric, recall@4, the gain is +2.6 to +3.4 and the pre-committed arm's 95% CI includes zero, so the registered bar is NOT met.
verdict.registered_bar: ci95_lo_pt > 0 AND delta_pt >= +2.0 on evidence_recall@4, n71433, 500 questions

pre_committed_single_arm.chosen_by: highest evidence_recall@4 on the 2,000 disjoint train questions (64.80)
pre_committed_single_arm.why: delta +2.60 clears the +2.0 point requirement but the 95% CI lower bound is -0.20, so the CI half of the bar fails

outcome_primary_metric_recall_at_4.multiplicity_note: 7 fusion families were tested; with a Bonferroni-adjusted interval no arm's recall@4 lower bound stays above zero (best is -0.40). The unadjusted per-arm bar is what was registered and is reported as such; the adjusted number is given because it is the more conservative reading, not as a replacement bar.

outcome_secondary_metric_recall_at_10.note: registered as a secondary metric before any number existed
outcome_secondary_metric_recall_at_10.reading: every fusion arm gains 5-6 points and survives multiplicity correction; the lexical arm reliably pulls gold evidence INTO the top 10 (best arm: 35 questions fixed against 4 broken) and is far less reliable about placing it in the top 4 (30 fixed against 16 broken).

bm25_alone.finding: lexical alone is NOT competitive on HotpotQA against nomic-embed-text: 25.2 points behind dense at recall@4 on the 71,433 corpus. The hybrid gain comes from COMPLEMENTARITY, not lexical strength -- BM25 is a minority vote that is right about different questions.

complementarity_evidence.reading: the lexical arm adds 3.0 points of candidate-pool ceiling the dense arm never returns at any depth up to 200. This is a property of the two scoring functions, measured with no fusion parameter involved.

corpus_size_dependence.reading: on the 1,190-doc corpus the dense top-200 already holds 100% of gold, so there is nothing for a lexical arm to add, and the transfer result is a clean negative (+1.67, CI [-5.00, +8.33]). The win appears only where the corpus is large enough for dense retrieval to crowd evidence out of the head.

cost_outcome.why: disk passes easily (50.4 MiB = 12.4% of the 406.2 MiB nanomem already writes for this corpus, limit was 25%); latency fails by 6% (1.0611 ms measured against the 1.0 ms limit). The measurement was taken while other benchmark processes ran on this machine. It is reported as a FAIL and was NOT re-measured to cross the line; a faster implementation must be re-measured against the same 1.0 ms limit before anyone claims a pass.

where_the_time_goes.note: the fusion merge is batch-shaped numpy call overhead on two 200-element lists, not algorithmic work

clean_negatives_reported: cascade cosine -> BM25 rerank: -9.80 at recall@4 (CI [-14.00, -5.60]); using BM25 as a re-ranker destroys the dense ordering it was handed
cascade BM25 -> cosine rerank: +0.80 at recall@4, CI includes zero; a lexical prefilter caps recall at BM25's own 83.0% pool ceiling

RRF: +1.00 at recall@4 (CI [-2.00, +4.00]); rank-only fusion discards the score margin the linear blends exploit, and its tuned constant was c=1, i.e. the sweep pushed it as far from standard RRF (c=60) as the grid allowed
val1190 transfer: +1.67 at recall@4, CI [-5.00, +8.33] -- not a win
BM25 alone: 25.2 points behind dense at recall@4

the exact-backfill variants, which remove the imputation entirely, did not beat the floored ones on the evaluation set (+2.60 vs +3.40 at recall@4): the imputation choice is worth less than the noise on 500 questions
verdict.recommendation: Do NOT integrate into nanomem on this evidence alone. What is proven: a mechanism-level complementarity (+3.0 points of candidate ceiling that does not depend on any tuned parameter) and a +5 to +6 point recall@10 gain that survives multiplicity correction. What is NOT proven: the registered recall@4 bar, and the query-latency limit was missed. The next step is a recall@10-shaped question -- does the chat pipeline consume a top-10? -- plus a re-measured query path, not another fusion sweep.
